Some files carry a notice of their own on top of that -- Linux's virtio_ring.h keeps Rusty Russell's and IBM's, boringssl keeps Sun's and Amazon's, libfdt keeps Kim Phillips's -- and those travel in the files, which is where the licences ask them to be. components.name: llvm
components.note: The compiler the delivery was built with, kept inside the component so one NOTICE and one manifest cover the whole thing. llvm-ar and llvm-ranlib fall here, along with anything a longer prefix does not claim -- and that catch-all is deliberate: nothing under toolchain/ may reach the root entry, which says GoldenRiver owns it. LLVM 7.0 predates the Apache-2.0-WITH-LLVM-exception relicensing, so this is the University of Illinois/NCSA Open Source License. clang and lld are separate subprojects with their own copyright lines and their own entries. The version and the triple are spelled out rather than templated: a toolchain bump should make the unclaimed-file gate fire, because it is the moment somebody has to look at these licences again.

components.name: libcxx
components.note: The C++ standard library headers. Every one carries the inline notice and points at a LICENSE.TXT the prebuilt does not contain. This is also the ABI boundary that makes the toolchain part of the delivery rather than a convenience: these headers build with _LIBCPP_ABI_VERSION 2, so the delivered archives mangle as std::__2 while a consumer's own upstream clang uses __1, and the two do not link.

components.name: libcxx-runtime
components.note: libc++.so, libc++abi.so and libunwind.so for the target. The sealed self-test's link traces name all three, which is why they are here and the sanitizer variants beside them are not.

components.embedded_reason: 107 of the 108 headers here are MIT and carry an individual author's copyright rather than the LLVM Team's; only opencl-c.h is NCSA, which is why the expression is AND and not OR. Each MIT header states the full permission notice inline, including the 'above copyright notice ... shall be included in all copies' clause, so shipping the file is itself what satisfies the attribution -- naming four individuals in the toolchain's own LICENSE text would misdescribe a text they did not write.
components.name: clang-builtin-headers
components.note: clang's builtin headers: stdint.h, stddef.h, the target intrinsics. Kept whole rather than filtered, because module.modulemap names every one of them and a resource directory that disagrees with its own modulemap is a failure mode nobody would look for.

components.name: compiler-rt
components.note: The compiler runtime. Only libclang_rt.builtins is kept: the link traces take five members of it -- addtf3, comparetf2, floatditf, multf3, subtf3, all software float128 -- and nothing from any other runtime library.
